title: Gluing affine quotients of a stable semistable open
statement: Let X be a projective finite-type scheme over a field k with an ample PGL-linearized invertible module L, in the sense of [def-sfb-pgl-linearized-polarization] and [def-sc-ample]. Let i:J→X be an open immersion identifying J on every algebraically closed extension with the semistable locus, and assume every such point of J is stable. For a coefficient map φ matching the structural constants, there is an invariant surjection q:J→Proj(E.invariantGrade) over k [def-pc-proj]. It is categorical for invariant maps to every algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], and induces a bijection between geometric orbits and geometric points. This statement does not assert finiteness or projectivity of the target.

source.place: MFK GIT Chapter 1 Theorem 1.10 and Appendix 1.C; Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3 Sections 8–9. The source-specific proof is written in the Lean docstring. Section-ring action uses Stacks 02KH; section finiteness uses Stacks 0B5T. Local MFK book is WANTED.

proof.text: Use the affine nonvanishing charts X_s of the polarized section ring. They lie in J and cover it. Restrict the action to them.

Identify R_(s) with the invariant ring of S_(s). Clear a power of s from the coaction defect of an invariant fraction; this argument permits zero divisors. Apply the affine finite-stabilizer geometric quotient theorem on each chart.
The fraction inclusions agree on X_(st), so glue the maps to Proj. Compute the inverse images of D_+(s) by the degree-zero fraction s^deg(t)/t^deg(s). Surjectivity and invariance follow chartwise.

Descend invariant maps uniquely on each target chart and glue by the algebraic-space sheaf condition. Use inverse-image equality and the affine orbit theorem for geometric point surjectivity and orbit fibres.

lean.statement:
theorem semistable_affine_quotient_gluing
    (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (hprojective : IsHProjective X.hom)
    (hfiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ QuasiCompact X.hom)
    (L : X.left.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hample : IsAmple X.hom L)
    (E : Action k r X L) (J : Over (Spec (.of k))) (i : J ⟶ X)
    (hopen : IsOpenImmersion i.left)
    (hss : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
      (x : fieldTest k Ω ⟶ X),
      E.IsSemistable Ω x ↔ ∃ y : fieldTest k Ω ⟶ J, y ≫ i = x)
    (hstable : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
      (x : fieldTest k Ω ⟶ J), E.IsStable Ω (x ≫ i))
    (φ : k →+* E.CoefficientRing)
    (hc : ∀ c : k, E.coefficientVal (φ c) = constantSection (Z := X) (L := L) c) :
    ∃ q : J ⟶ E.projOver φ,
      Surjective q.left ∧
      (∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (g : Matrices k r T) (x y : T ⟶ J),
        y ≫ i = E.act T g (x ≫ i) → y ≫ q = x ≫ q) ∧
      (∀ (B : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (f : yoneda.obj J ⟶ B.obj.obj),
        E.IsInvariantMap i B f →
          ∃! a : yoneda.obj (E.projOver φ) ⟶ B.obj.obj, yoneda.map q ≫ a = f) ∧
      (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω],
        Function.Surjective (fun x : fieldTest k Ω ⟶ J ↦ x ≫ q) ∧
        ∀ x y : fieldTest k Ω ⟶ J,
          (x ≫ q = y ≫ q ↔ ∃ g : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin r) Ω,
            E.act _ (fieldMatrix Ω g) (x ≫ i) = y ≫ i))
